newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G calls for N.J. utils emissions rule.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G calls for N.J. utils emissions rule.

text.p: Public Service Electric & Gas Co said Friday it has asked the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU) to impose a rule requiring all power providers in the state to periodically disclose their emission rates.
The proposal, filed with the BPU today, is designed to protect New Jersey's air quality from such pollutants as nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide particulates, PSE&G said in a statement.
"Deregulation is an important step for New Jersey, but opening our markets shouldn't mean opening our borders to dirty air," President and Chief Operating Officer Lawrence Codey said.

In addition to the monitoring process, PSE&G said it wants BPU to require those companies whose systemwide rates exceed state rates to obtain a sufficient number of emission credits that can be traded to offset the higher rates from the out-of-state sources.
PSE&G's proposal is in addition to the utility's final comments given to the BPU by the Feb 28 deadline as part of the state's electricity restructuring process.
PSE&G said it is actively working toward the goal of providing a rate reduction of five to 10 percent for all New Jersey customers.
The state's restructuring plan is slated to be complete by April 2001.
PSE&G also urged the BPU to avoid using a "one-size-fits-all" philosophy in restructuring the industry by opening up the generation market in steps to avoid damaging system reliability.
PSE&G, a unit of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc., is the state's largest regulated utility and serves about 75 percent of its population.
